subject: Peakhours model profiles & capacity handoff - FinWave PoC
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Peakhours model profiles & capacity handoff - FinWave PoC

Hi Samira —

Following our kickoff, here's the initial model shortlist + a conservative workload sizing sketch so your infra and SRE teams can preview requirements before the PoC. I included Ben, Grace and Monica for ops/CS alignment. Please confirm the assumptions below or send the sample traffic you mentioned and we'll refine.

Quick summary / ask:
- Goal: support document Q&A + extractive summarization across full financial filings (upload + conversational fallback).
- Primary constraints: many long documents (typical single-request context needed: 20k-40k tokens), latency target for interactive flows ~800ms median at 95th for short queries, POC target throughput ~150 QPS peak across tenants.

Model shortlist (quality vs cost/latency tradeoffs):
1) Llama-2-chat-70b-32k (quantized 8-bit): best balance for long-context Q&A; higher GPU memory but good latency with batching.
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (32k variant via context windowing + retrieval): lower cost; recommend when you augment with retrieval and chunking.
3) Falcon-40B-instruct (16k): mid-tier option if most requests are <=16k.
4) Open long-context LLM (hybrid approach): host a smaller low-latency model for short prompts and route long-context calls to the 70k/32k variant.

Traffic & token assumptions (please validate with your sample):
- Expected PoC footprint (conservative): 100k requests / month
- Avg prompt tokens (incl. doc snippets): 1,200
- Avg completion tokens: 600
- Avg tokens / request: ~1,800 -> monthly = ~180M tokens
- Peak traffic: 150 QPS for a 20-minute window during market hours (9:30–9:50am PT)
- Concurrency (steady-state outside peak): 8–15 RPS

Operational knobs we recommend enabling in the PoC:
- KV/prefix caching for common system prompts (+ expected 20% token reduction if you can cache stable preambles).
- Aggressive batching for background summaries (non-interactive flows).
- Retrieval + chunking with 4–8KB chunk size to reduce full-context costs when feasible.

Preliminary capacity recommendation for POC:
- If using Llama-2-chat-70b-32k (quantized): start with 4x high-memory GPUs (e.g., each configured to serve ~35–45 RPS depending on batching and quantization) and add autoscale headroom.
- If using Mistral-Instruct-7B (cost-first): 2–3 GPUs with caching and retrieval should meet the same latency budget.

Next steps (requested from FinWave):
1) Share 48–72 hrs of representative traffic (headers + token lengths) — preferably the CSV you mentioned.
2) Confirm latency SLOs for the two user flows (interactive Q&A vs background summarization).
3) Approve a sizing call this week (30m) to lock final GPU count and rollout path.

Attachments: I attached a sizing template and sample MAP we use for PoCs.

Thanks — happy to review live.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Samira Khan <samira@finwave.ai>

Subject: Re: Peakhours model profiles & capacity handoff - FinWave PoC

Thanks Vanessa — this is super helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 20k-40k context estimate is correct for our full filings Q&A flow (users often paste entire 10–20 page reports). For the first wave we can target a 32k context window; anything >32k should use retrieval/chunking.
- For monthly traffic, the 100k requests is accurate for the PoC + some early beta customers. Production could be 1M+/mo but that's 2028 work.
- Peak window is usually 9:30–10:00 ET (so ~2:30–3:00am PT) — but you'll be seeing European daytime spikes too occasionally.

I attached the anonymized traffic sample (headers + token counts) and a short doc listing our two main flows. Can you also confirm estimated monthly token cost ballpark for the two model choices (70b vs Mistral-7B) so procurement has an order-of-magnitude cost?

Samira
Head of Product
FinWave Analytics
samira@finwave.ai

Attachment: finwave-traffic-sample.csv
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Peakhours model profiles & capacity handoff - FinWave PoC

Samira — thanks for the sample, that clarifies things a lot. Attached is a filled sizing template (redwood-sizing-template.xlsx) and a quick cost sketch. High-level numbers below (ballpark, excluding infra discounts / reserved commit):

Cost sketch (monthly, approximate):
- Llama-2-chat-70b-32k (quantized + dedupe): ~ $12k–$18k / month for the PoC token consumption (180M tokens), plus GPU hosting if you self-host. With Redwood hosted pricing + reserved capacity we can get to lower unit costs — I asked Sales/Finance to model a committed tier for you.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B + retrieval: ~ $4k–$6k / month for the same token volume (retrieval may increase token count slightly due to context augmentation but lowers model cost per-token).

Operational notes based on the traffic sample:
- Median request tokens trimmed to ~1,100 after aggressive chunking; a subset (~12%) still needs full 32k windows.
- We expect a 15–22% token reduction from prefix caching across the most frequent system prompts in your sample.
- Peak concurrency from your CSV aligns with ~135–160 QPS 95th in a 10–15 minute market-synced spike.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) We'll provision a temporary PoC pool (dedicated) sized to the 4-GPU Llama-70b configuration while we run a short AB test with Mistral-7B + retrieval to compare latency and cost.
2) Schedule a 30-minute sizing/procurement call — proposed: Fri 2027-09-17 10:00am ET. Ben, can you join to cover Dedicated capacity and pricing?

I've uploaded the filled template and a one-page MAP to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/finwave/PoC-MAP

— Vanessa

Thanks — I'll jump on the Friday call. Quick notes from infra/pricing side:

- I'll prepare two committed-tier scenarios (12-month vs 3-month) and a run-rate comparison (hosted Redwood vs customer-managed GPUs) by tomorrow EOD.
- For the PoC, we recommend enabling autoscale + burst to handle the 10–15 min market spikes instead of steady provisioning for peak. That gives better cost/performance for the POC.
